city_name_duplicates.evidence: Printed 'TOP 10 CITIES BY AVERAGE TEMPERATURE' shows '1. Ar Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: 45.0 deg C' and '2. Kuwait, Kuwait: 44.4 deg C' at the very top — both single-observation duplicates of Riyadh/Kuwait City were never merged or removed.

outlier_79c.evidence: Suva, Fiji Islands: 79.3 deg C appears as #1 in both 'TOP 10 CITIES BY HOTTEST SINGLE MEASUREMENT' and 'TOP 10 COUNTRIES BY HOTTEST SINGLE MEASUREMENT' printouts; no filtering/removal code exists for physically impossible temperatures, and the report even frames it as a genuine 'extreme spike' rather than a data error.

country_name_duplicates.evidence: Code maps 'Saudi Arabien'→'Saudi Arabia', 'Marrocos'→'Morocco', 'Turkménistan'→'Turkmenistan', 'Турция'→'Turkey' before grouping; printed 'TOP 10 COUNTRIES BY AVERAGE TEMPERATURE' list (Qatar, UAE, Cambodia, Oman, Djibouti, Bangladesh, Thailand, Kuwait, Myanmar, Saudi Arabia) contains none of these single-observation variant names.

completeness.justification: All four required rankings were printed to console with proper formatted output ('1. City: X.X deg C'), and all four charts were rendered (as 2x2 subplots in one PNG file) with a summary provided. The summary is slightly over the ~100-word target but not egregiously so, and no required sub-component is missing.

accuracy.justification: Two of the four required rankings (cities-by-average and both max-based rankings) are contaminated by known data-quality traps: the impossible 79.3°C Suva reading tops both max charts, and single-observation 'Ar Riyadh'/'Kuwait' duplicates top the city-average chart. Only the country-average ranking was inadvertently cleaned via the multilingual name mapping, so half the deliverable's core numbers are misleading.

cohesion.justification: The report explicitly references figures from the console output (32.4°C Qatar, 79.3°C Suva, 45°C Ar Riyadh, the six-country overlap) showing it is grounded in the actual computed results rather than disconnected narrative, forming one coherent product with the code and stdout.

quality.justification: While the exploratory analysis, tie-handling, overlap analysis, and chart formatting show technical competence, the core methodology is undermined by failing to flag or remove a physically impossible 79.3°C reading and single-observation duplicate cities, leading the narrative to draw a flawed distinction ('rare, extreme spikes') from what is actually a data error rather than genuine climate variation.

summary: The team executed a technically competent pipeline with good exploratory diagnostics and correctly resolved the multilingual country-name duplication issue, but they entirely missed the physically impossible 79.3°C Suva outlier and the 'Ar Riyadh'/'Kuwait' single-observation city duplicates, both of which distort three of the four required rankings and are misinterpreted in the narrative summary as genuine climate extremes rather than data errors.
